reasoning: I agree with the Market Analyst's neutral stance: SPY is 5.7% above its 200-day, but tech and communication are rolling over, defensives lead, and the Fed decision (10-28) plus three mega-cap reports land this week. The account is about 85% invested with 14.7% cash, so idle cash does count against us, but neither proposal has a strong enough edge to justify full size into the event. MSM is a clean, event-clear, 9/9 F-score name with low beta (0.72), so I keep it but halve it because the Skeptic and Implicator are right that it is an industrial-distribution peer of FAST (same MRO theme, not a new sector) and the Market Analyst says to avoid Industrials. VXUS is rejected for now: it is below its 200-day, has a beta of 1.11 (it would not cushion a drawdown), emerging-market stress (EWZ -21%, China AI rout) is still unfolding, and the proposer concedes it is not a conviction call, so nothing is lost by waiting a day for the Fed. Lesson L1 shaped the MSM stop: it is anchored to the actual fill, not the stale 10-22 menu close, because the post-print price reaction is unknown. L2 was satisfied for MSM (8-K 2.02 and 10-K filed 10-22, next earnings about 2027-01-06). Cash after this trade is roughly 13%, which leaves room to add diversification (VXUS or similar) after the Fed if the trend holds.

trades.thesis: Quality industrial distributor: 9/9 F-score, cash flow $306M vs net income $223M, newest 10-K on the menu, already reported on 10-22 so no earnings event in the window, low beta (0.72). Sized small (about 1.3% of equity) because it overlaps FAST's industrial-MRO exposure, profitability (gp 0.65) is the weakest on the analyst's list, and the Market Analyst tilts away from Industrials.
trades.invalidation: Close more than about 9% below the actual fill price (re-anchor to the fill, not the $118.72 menu close; roughly $108 only if it fills near the menu close), or a new 8-K showing a guidance cut or restatement of the FY2026 results.

rejected.why: The Skeptic's case is stronger than the proposal. VXUS is already below its 200-day (-0.41%) and the Market Analyst prefers broad US exposure over international, which we already hold through VOO and VTI. The Implicator confirms it has a beta of 1.11, higher than VOO and VTI, so it diversifies geography but not drawdown risk, and the Brazil and China rout is still unfolding. The proposer calls it not a conviction call, and the invalidation level is inconsistent (80.0 is about 3.6% below the 200-day, not 3%). With the Fed decision tomorrow there is no cost to waiting for a post-meeting close above the 200-day before adding non-US exposure.
